name: docs-python
description: Official Python documentation (docs.python.org, a static Sphinx site). The CLI fetches the glossary as JSON, the module index, the general index by letter, tables of contents, What's New highlights, doc pages, the API entries on a page, and documentation downloads, for any docs version.

commands.name: get-glossary
commands.summary: Get every Python glossary term with its HTML definition, as a JSON object keyed by term

params.name: version
params.description: Docs version: '3' (latest stable) or a specific version such as '3.12' or '3.13'

commands.name: list-modules
commands.summary: List all standard-library modules from the Python Module Index, with descriptions and doc links

commands.name: get-index-letter
commands.summary: List general index entries (functions, classes, keywords, topics) that start with a given letter, with links to where each is documented

params.name: letter
params.description: Uppercase index letter A-Z, or 'Symbols' or '_'

commands.name: list-toc
commands.summary: List the table of contents (chapters and pages) of a docs section such as the library reference, tutorial, HOWTOs, language reference or What's New

commands.name: get-page
commands.summary: Get a documentation page (module reference, tutorial chapter, HOWTO, What's New) with its title, breadcrumb, source link and full text

params.name: section
params.description: Docs section directory, e.g. library, tutorial, howto, reference, whatsnew, builtins

commands.source: E5 E7 E8 E13 E19 E20 E21 E22 E23 E24 E25 E26 E27 E28 E29 E30 E37 GET https://docs.python.org/{n}/library/asyncio-task.html

commands.name: get-api-entries
commands.summary: List the API objects (functions, classes, methods, attributes, exceptions, data) documented on a page, each with signature, anchor and first description paragraph
commands.source: E17 E19 E26 E27 E28 E16 GET https://docs.python.org/{n}/library/asyncio-queue.html

commands.name: get-release-highlights
commands.summary: Get the 'Summary – Release highlights' bullet points from a Python release's What's New page

params.name: version
params.description: Docs version to read from: '3' (latest) or e.g. '3.12'

commands.source: E2 E3 E4 E9 E12 E15 E31 E34 GET https://docs.python.org/{n}/whatsnew/3.11.html

commands.name: list-downloads
commands.summary: List downloadable documentation archives (PDF, HTML, plain text, EPUB) for a docs version

notes: Full-text search (search.html) runs in the browser against searchindex.js, so the server returns no results. To find things, use list-modules, get-index-letter (general index by letter), get-glossary or list-toc, then get-page.
The version path param accepts '3' (latest stable, currently 3.15) or a specific version such as '3.12'. Translations use a language prefix in the URL, e.g. /fr/3/ (not exposed as a param).

Links in results are relative to the page, e.g. 'library/json.html#module-json' from the module index, or 'asyncio-task.html#asyncio.Task' from a library page. To call get-page, split the link into section (directory) and page (file name without .html).
get-page returns the full page text in 'content', which can be large. Use get-api-entries for a compact list of the functions and classes on a reference page.
Glossary bodies are HTML fragments, and their links are relative to glossary.html.
